## setting
**197 run(s)** — rule `var19-setting` — 10.1073/pnas.1907500116  
*Abstract and Significance*

> We grew 2 cultivars of the naturally drought-tolerant food crop sorghum in the field under drought stress. We sequenced the mRNA from weekly samples of these plants, resulting in a molecular profile of drought response over the growing season. ... We profiled almost 400 transcriptomes sampled weekly from leaves and roots of 2 genotypes (the preflowering drought-tolerant RTx430 and the stay-green type BTx642), under control watering conditions and 2 different drought regimes. ... Paired-end RNA-Seq was performed on 198 root and 198 leaf samples (396 samples total).

## tissue
**197 run(s)** — rule `var19-tissue` — 10.1073/pnas.1907500116  
*GEO GSE128441 sample records, cached at studies/doi_10.1073_pnas.1907500116/GSE128441_samples.txt*

> SRA holds no tissue, location or date for any of the 395 runs; GEO holds all of it. Per sample: source_name is Leaves (197) or Roots (198); characteristics give genotype, watering regime, age in days and plot; molecule is 'polyA RNA' on all 395, which epicon_runs.py REFUSES to proceed without. The second description line is a 10-character code whose first six digits are MMDDYY, resolving to 16 weekly timepoints from 2016-06-15 to 2016-09-28. Genotypes RTX430 197 / BTX642 198; regimes Control 162 / Preflowering drought 150 / Postflowering drought 83. Joins 395/395 of our runs on SampleName, which is the GSM accession.

## location
**197 run(s)** — rule `var19-location` — 10.1073/pnas.1907500116  
*2026 companion paper, Methods 'Growth conditions and drought treatment' (PMC12863931)*

> The 2019 paper's main text does not name the field site; it is in the SI Appendix, whose Europe PMC supplementary zip is truncated and unreadable. The site comes instead from the group's 2026 multi-season companion paper, which names it and states that year 1 followed the same protocol: 'Sorghum plants were planted, grown, and treated as described by Varoquaux et al. (2019) with some differences in years 2 and 3. These included, for year 2, plants being sown in pre-wetted plots at Kearny Agricultural Research and Extension Center (Parlier, CA, USA) on June 6th, 2017'. NOT taken from the author affiliations, which also list Kearney: an affiliation is where an author works, not where a plant grew.
